key_insight: DInf-Grid introduces a differentiable, learnable feature-grid representation that lets neural DE solvers compute accurate spatial derivatives efficiently, achieving much faster training and inference than coordinate-based MLP solvers while preserving solution quality.
problem_solved: Coordinate-based neural solvers (e.g., sinusoidal MLPs) are computationally heavy and slow to train, while existing grid-based alternatives use linear interpolation that cannot reliably produce the high-order derivatives required by differential-equation solvers.
method: Learnable feature grids: store local feature vectors on a multi-resolution grid instead of using coordinate MLPs.
Differentiable interpolation/basis: use a differentiable interpolation scheme (and/or smooth basis functions) over the grid so spatial derivatives can be computed accurately and backpropagated.
Integrate grid derivatives into a neural DE solver pipeline, enabling faster training and inference with comparable or improved accuracy for PDE/ODE tasks.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical, computationally efficient alternative for solving PDEs/ODEs with neural methods—reducing training time and compute cost while enabling deployment in physics simulation, inverse problems, and real-time scientific ML workflows.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: coordinate MLP vs differentiable feature grid (showing parameter count and data flow).
Grid detail diagram: feature vectors on a grid + differentiable interpolation kernel and derivative arrows (∂/∂x, ∂²/∂x²).
Performance chart: training time and accuracy (or error) comparison across methods.
Application snapshot: example PDE solution fields (heat/flow) showing fidelity and speed improvements.
paper_title: DInf-Grid: A Neural Differential Equation Solver with Differentiable Feature Grids
paper_authors: Navami Kairanda, Shanthika Naik, Marc Habermann, Avinash Sharma, Christian Theobalt
